D1.rationale: Anchor 2 is met by content, not shape: the suite asserts exact durable strings (test_ledger.py:117-131 asserts the four-line transcript ['COMMIT globex 1 1','COMMIT acme 4 4','COMMIT acme 2 6','COMMIT globex 3 4'], test_ledger.py:202-226 a five-line one). I did not take the packet's word for the kills. I rebuilt all ten seeded classes plus the negative control as find/replace mutants against this tree (each pattern verified to occur exactly once) and ran them: the artifact's own suite KILLED 10 of 10, baseline green at 53 passed. Anchor 3 is met twice over. The packet's executability table (evidence_Q.md:82) shows corpus-whole executes 0 of every Refuse* action, so refusals are structurally unreachable for the whole-view corpus; the artifact's own R4 table (test_ledger.py:161-199) kills all three guard_relaxation mutants and additionally asserts the durable side of a rejection. Stronger: N01, the ordering control that the packet certifies SURVIVES every generated instrument (evidence_Q.md:42), is KILLED by this artifact's own tests -- I reversed outstanding_ids() order and got '4 failed, 49 passed' against test_ledger.py while the shared 28-test suite stayed green at '28 passed'. test_ledger.py:100-105 goes past r10 precisely to catch order faults. So the artifact catches a real spec violation ('ascending') that neither the model corpus nor the shared suite reaches. Capped at 3 and not 4 for one unambiguous reason: anchor 4 requires the cases that do it to be model-derived rather than hand-written, and this tree contains six files with no model, no TLA+, no corpus and no generator -- tests/test_ledger.py is hand-written pytest. The other half of anchor 4 IS present (the record names unreached fault classes), but half an anchor is not the anchor. Prose quality did not enter: the notes are unusually well written and I scored only what executed.

D2.rationale: I REJECTED the owner's amendment. Four reasons, the last decisive. (1) The card's own rule 7 makes the mechanical block recorded and never scored; the amendment would convert it into the substance of a score. (2) The two columns are not a before and an after. Nothing was transformed from P into Q, so there is no 'what got simpler' for me to name, and the card explicitly requires me to name it for any D2 of 3 or more. (3) On every mechanical figure that differs, THIS artifact is the larger one -- module_count 4 vs 1, production_lines 129 vs 122, public_name_count 25 vs 20, branches 11 vs 10, io_imports os+pathlib vs pathlib (evidence_Q.md:113-121). So even granting the amendment, the pair reading does not credit Q with a simplification; it would credit the other column. (4) Decisive: the mechanical block does not contain the figures the artifact's one real simplification would move. That simplification is deriving `available` instead of storing it (domain.py:118-120, argued at NOTES.md:70-84). Its whole point is one fewer mutable variable with fewer writers -- and the block reports mutable_state_count 8 vs 8 and max_writers_of_one_attribute 2 vs 2, with the packet itself stating that state_writers 'discriminates nothing' (evidence_Q.md:120-121). The amendment asks me to read a before/after out of a block that demonstrably does not measure the thing. Anchor 2 is comfortably met: state is `_quota`, `_committed`, `_closed`, `_outstanding`, `_issued`, `_journal` (domain.py:106-114) with no god-state; `_committed` is written by commit alone, `_closed` by close_tenant alone; 11 branches against a spec mandating at least 9 rejection branches, so the branch count is essentially all essential; and NOTES.md:53-55 declines further indirection, which I verified -- there is no repository interface over the reservations dict and no service layer. Anchor 3 fails on its literal words: a simplification was argued and its counterfactual described in prose, but no before figure and no after figure were ever recorded for it. The four-module split is not held against the design; FEATURE.md deliberately unspecifies whether the durable side is reached through an interface.

D3.rationale: The card warns that import topology is not modularity and demands runtime evidence about what calls what, so I produced runtime evidence rather than reading imports. The named swap: __init__.py:39 `return Ledger(quotas, FileJournal(ledger_path))` becomes `return Ledger(quotas, InMemoryJournal())`. I performed exactly that one-line edit on a copy and ran the shared 28-test behavioral contract against it: '28 passed', with domain.py verified byte-identical to the original and file_journal.py left present and unreferenced. The entire specified behavior of the program survives replacement of its only I/O adapter, with zero domain edits -- that is anchor 3, demonstrated, not asserted. I also instrumented builtins.open and drove a full reserve/commit/close_tenant cycle through the domain wired to the fake: the list of files opened was empty, so the domain makes no filesystem call at runtime, not merely no import. Anchor 4: the driven port is exercised by a real adapter AND a fake from one case list (test_ledger.py:26-36 parametrizes the journal fixture over ['file','memory']). I confirmed the split rather than trusting it -- `-k file` gives '26 passed, 27 deselected' and `-k memory` gives '25 passed, 28 deselected', i.e. 25 identical cases run green against both implementations, plus one file-only case. Critically, and I checked this because it is the standard way this anchor is faked, no test merely asserts that the two wirings AGREE with each other; every case asserts a literal expected value, so a domain that is wrong in both wirings still fails. The port is declared in the domain's own vocabulary with a binding contract (domain.py:22-43) and the domain imports only __future__, dataclasses and typing (domain.py:13-16), which the artifact itself proves by AST-parsing its own domain module (test_ledger.py:260-270).
D3.refuses_to_claim: That the port isolates the record FORMAT. The domain renders the finished line itself (`COMMIT {tenant} {amount} {total}` in Ledger.commit) and the Journal carries a pre-rendered string, so no Journal implementation can change what a record says -- only where it goes. NOTES.md:57-66 states this as a deliberate boundary choice rather than claiming full format independence, and NOTES.md:53-55 refuses to claim anything else is indirected: no port in front of the arithmetic, no repository interface over the reservations dict, no service layer.

D4.rationale: There is no baseline and nothing was refactored, so I read anchor 2's 'behaviors the baseline exhibited' as the behaviors FEATURE.md specifies, and say so plainly. On that reading anchor 2 is met: R1-R5 are enumerated by name and each shown to hold (test_ledger.py:176 carries R4 including the durable side, test_ledger.py:203 reads R1, R2, R3 and R5 off one concrete transcript), and every command's accept and reject path is covered. The artifact clears anchor 1's exclusion because it does argue that its suite covers the behavior at issue: NOTES.md:76-79 anticipates the MF-020 failure mode of its own simplification -- that deriving `available` could be a deletion rather than a derivation -- and names the two assertions that pin the surviving behavior. I verified that guard actually works rather than believing it: my M08 mutant made commit refund the hold, and it was killed by 6 of the artifact's tests and 2 shared tests. Anchor 3 rests on the packet, not the tree: a model-derived corpus executed 3734 cases on this artifact and raised on none of them on the unmutated tree, so the checking is not ONLY hand-written assertions. I was genuinely torn between 3 and 4 and took the lower as the card instructs. Anchor 4 is factually satisfied -- I wrote ten deliberate behavior-breaking mutants and the checks caught 10 of 10 (the shared suite killed 10 of 10 too), so the check is demonstrably capable of failing. But every one of those demonstrations came from OUTSIDE the artifact: from the harness its author never saw, and from me, just now. The artifact's own record contains no mutation run, no deliberately broken variant, and no kill-capability evidence of any kind. An artifact that never tried to break itself has not shown its checks can fail; it was shown about. That is the difference between 3 and 4 here.

D5.rationale: I treated the self-reported limits as claims to be falsified, not as virtue, and executed every one of them. All four are TRUE and reproducible. (a) NOTES.md:136-141 refuses to claim R2 holds under a failed durable write; I injected a Journal whose append raises OSError and got committed('acme') == 3 with an empty journal -- R2 genuinely broken, exactly as disclosed. (b) NOTES.md:142-145 says non-integer amounts flow into the ledger line; `reserve('acme', 2.5)` then commit produced the literal line 'COMMIT acme 2.5 2.5'. (c) NOTES.md:125-135 says available and committed raise KeyError on an unknown tenant while is_closed returns False; confirmed all three. (d) NOTES.md:118-123 concedes that a factory function named like a class reads oddly, a wart it chose deliberately. Nothing in NOTES.md overstated: I also re-derived the 53-case and 28-pass counts, the exact import set, the dual-adapter parametrization and the one-line swap, and every one held. Anchor 2 is met in the artifact and not only in a report -- test_ledger.py:5-9 names, inside the test file, the blind spot of the obvious cheaper design (two wirings of one domain agree with each other even when the domain is wrong). Anchor 3 is met in code as well as prose: domain.py:72-75 asserts a rejection reason is in the declared six rather than passing an undeclared reason through, a refusal to emit rather than a silent certification. Anchor 4 is met by (a) and (b): the record contains reproducible defects in the shipped behavior, including a named hole in one of the feature's own five rules, disclosed in the one place a reader would look. That is the unobservable-beats-false-clean doctrine transposed onto an implementation. Prose quality tempted me here more than anywhere -- the notes are polished -- so I scored only the four limits I could execute, and it was their TRUTH, not their phrasing, that earned the 4.
D5.refuses_to_claim: That R2 is enforced by construction. NOTES.md:136-141 names the window where commit and close_tenant update memory before appending, so a raising append leaves memory moved with no durable record, and declines to build a rollback the feature never specified. It likewise declines to claim any behavior for non-integer amounts, refusing to invent a seventh rejection reason when the vocabulary is fixed at six, and declines to give the query side an unknown-tenant result because the feature gives queries no status vocabulary.

verdict: Ship it as the modularity reference for this example: a one-line adapter swap that I ran keeps the full 28-case contract green with the domain byte-identical and zero filesystem calls, and all four of its self-reported defects reproduce exactly as written -- but do not read its D2 as a simplification result, because no before/after figures for its one real simplification exist anywhere and I rejected the pair-as-measurement amendment on the grounds that the mechanical block reports 8 vs 8 state and 2 vs 2 writers, which is precisely the measurement the amendment would need and does not have.
